hypothesis: Repair flips correlate positively with score (rho=+0.41) and the quadratic balance term is flat near 50%, so the raw partition drifts and the official repair mangles the learned critical structure; scaling the balance coefficient 10 -> 20 (modest x2, no new mechanism) lands the raw area ratio closer to 0.5 and reduces how much the repair step has to move, preserving the Laplacian's critical-pair locality.
analysis:
(1) No. Repair flips rose (103→118) rather than falling, and crit_cross worsened on C1 (0.011→0.016); the x2 balance scaling did not reduce repair movement as predicted.

(2) C1 drove the gain (score +0.080, dWNS +10.3%) despite higher cut/wcut and crit_cross—so improvement isn't from preserved critical-pair locality; C2 regressed (-0.032), C3 flat. Mechanism unclear/contradicts hypothesis.

(3) No: seed_std=0.049 with robust mean -0.033 and min_case -0.032—gains are seed-fragile, not robust.

(4) Ablate balance coefficient (10/15/20) on C1 alone, logging raw area ratio and repair_flips, to test whether the C1 gain is causal or noise.
